rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham answered his father’s idolatry with monotheistic proof and gentle exhortation, while his father answered with imitation, insult, and threat; God recounts this to comfort Muhammad amid polytheist abuse.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن إبراهيم عليه السلام لما دعا أباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the father’s question is genuine, it is futile because he already knew from repeated admonition that Abraham rejected the idols.
rows.anchor: فإن كان ذلك على وجه الاستفهام فهو خذلان لأنه قد عرف منه ما تكرر منه من وعظه وتنبيهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the father speaks in amazement, the real cause for amazement is rational people worshipping idols, not rejecting an argument that disproves them.
rows.anchor: وإن كان ذلك على سبيل التعجب فأي تعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father’s baseless astonishment countered Abraham’s reasoned astonishment that an intelligent person would worship idols.
rows.anchor: ذلك التعجب الظاهر المبني على الدليل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says rajm throughout the Qur’an means verbal abuse, insult, or blame.
rows.anchor: الرجم في القرآن كله بمعنى الشتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes rajm literally as throwing stones by hand.
rows.anchor: أنه الرجم باليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported interpretation is that the father would expose Abraham to the people so they would stone and kill him.
rows.anchor: لأرجمنك بإظهار أمرك للناس ليرجموك ويقتلوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the father would stone Abraham to make him go far away.
rows.anchor: لأرجمنك بالحجارة لتتباعد عني

rows.speaker: المؤرج
rows.claim: Al-Mu’arrij says rajm means “I will kill you” in Quraysh dialect.
rows.anchor: عن المؤرج لأقتلنك بلغة قريش

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim reads rajm as stoning, extended figuratively to expulsion and distance; the following command to leave supports expulsion.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم لأرجمنك المراد منه الرجم بالحجارة إلا أنه قد يقال ذلك في معنى الطرد والإبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basic sense of rajm is pelting with stones, so the literal sense is preferable; “leave me” does not prove verbal insult because it tells Abraham to flee the threat.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن أصل الرجم هو الرمي بالرجام فحمله عليه أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Leave me” is interpreted either as ending speech or as physically leaving the house and country, as the Messenger and believers migrated.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : المراد واهجرني بالقول . والثاني : بالمفارقة في الدار والبلد وهي هجرة الرسول والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Physical separation from the father is closer to the apparent meaning of the command.
rows.anchor: وهذا الثاني أقرب إلى الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of maliyyan means for a long time, from the expression for a long stretch of time.
rows.anchor: مليا أي مدة بعيدة مأخوذ من قولهم أتى على فلان ملاوة من الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading means leave while still able to go, before the father beats and incapacitates him; the word can mean capable and able.
rows.anchor: عني والهجران قبل أن أثخنك بالضرب حتى لا تقدر أن تبرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordination “and leave me” omits an implied “beware me,” supplied by the threat of stoning: beware me and leave lest I stone you.
rows.anchor: عطف اهجرني على معطوف عليه محذوف يدل عليه لأرجمنك ، أي فاحذرني واهجرني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s “peace be on you” is a farewell and truce, like the replies in al-Qasas and al-Furqan.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { سلام عليك } توادع ومتاركة كقوله تعالى : { لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم سلام عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This supports disengaging from an advised person who persists obstinately and answering abuse with kindness.
rows.anchor: وهذا دليل على جواز متاركة المنصوح إذا ظهر منه اللجاج ، وعلى أنه تحسن مقابلة الإساءة بالإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Abraham prayed for his father’s safety to win him over, as shown by the accompanying promise to seek forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون قد دعا له بالسلامة استمالة له ، ألا ترى أنه وعده بالاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although he leaves, Abraham’s concern for his father remains, as his promise to seek forgiveness shows.
rows.anchor: ضم إلى ذلك ما دل به على أنه وإن بعد عنه فاشفاقه باق عليه كما كان

rows.speaker: من طعن في عصمة الأنبياء
rows.claim: Critics argue that Abraham sinned by seeking forgiveness for his unbelieving father, since the Qur’an and consensus establish the father’s unbelief and forbid seeking forgiveness for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: واحتج بهذه الآية من طعن في عصمة الأنبياء ، وتقريره أن إبراهيم عليه السلام فعل ما لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First reply: certainty that God will punish a disbeliever depends on revelation; Abraham’s law may not have established that certainty.
rows.anchor: أن القطع على أن الله تعالى يعذب الكافر لا يعرف إلا بالسمع ، فلعل إبراهيم عليه السلام لم يجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second reply: seeking forgiveness may mean asking God to spare the father immediate worldly punishment while he lived, as in al-Jathiya.
rows.anchor: أن الاستغفار قد يكون بمعنى الاستماحة ، كما في قوله : { قل للذين ءامنوا يغفروا للذين لا يرجون أيام الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third reply: Abraham hoped his father would believe; his law may have permitted praying for a disbeliever expected to believe, and the ban applies after knowing someone is destined for Hell.
rows.anchor: إنما استغفر لأبيه لأنه كان يرجو منه الإيمان فلما أيس من ذلك ترك الاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tawba explains that Abraham’s promise was conditional on his father believing; when the father did not believe, Abraham ceased and disavowed him.
rows.anchor: وما كان استغفار إبراهيم لابيه إلا عن موعدة وعدها إياه فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on taking Abraham as an example in this act does not prove it was sinful, since prophets can have lawful acts that are special to them.
rows.anchor: لكن المنع من التأسي به في ذلك لا يدل على أن ذلك كان معصية . فإن كثيرا من الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth reply is that the prayer may have been a permissible but less-preferred act, as good deeds of the righteous can be shortcomings for those nearest to God.
rows.anchor: لعل هذا الاستغفار كان من باب ترك الأولى وحسنات الأبرار سيئآت المقربين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafiyyan means gentle, gracious, and exceptionally kind, from the idiom for treating a petitioner gently, as in Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أي لطيفا رفيقا يقال أحفى فلان في المسألة بفلان إذا لطف به وبالغ في الرفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s kindness and generosity had accustomed Abraham to answered prayers, so he speaks as confident that repentance would bring his father forgiveness.
rows.anchor: لطفه بي وإنعامه على عودني الإجابة فإذا أنا استغفرت لك حصل المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham will separate both geographically and religiously from his people and their idols, worshipping the Lord who creates and benefits rather than harmful idols.
rows.anchor: أفارقكم في المكان وأفارقكم في طريقتكم أيضا وأبعد عنكم وأتشاغل بعبادة ربي الذي ينفع ويضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I hope not to be wretched in calling my Lord” expresses humility, as does Abraham’s “I hope” in al-Shu‘ara.
rows.anchor: أرجو أن لا أكون كذلك ، وإنما ذكر ذلك على سبيل التواضع كقوله : { والذى أطمع أن يغفر لى خطيئتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling on his Lord also insinuates that his people are wretched for calling on idols, which cannot hear or benefit anyone.
rows.anchor: تعريض بشقاوتهم في دعاء آلهتهم على ما قرره أولا في / قوله : { لم * تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s religious and physical separation and migration did not cost him in religion or worldly life; God compensated him with prophetic sons.
rows.anchor: لما اعتزلهم في دينهم وفي بلدهم واختار الهجرة إلى ربه إلى حيث أمره لم يضره ذلك دينا ودنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being made a messenger whom people must obey is among the highest worldly and afterlife blessings.
rows.anchor: ولا حالة في الدين والدنيا للبشر أرفع من أن يجعل الله له رسولا إلى خلقه ويلزم الخلق طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy to them includes prophecy and can also include wealth, status, followers, pure lineage, and good descendants.
rows.anchor: وهب لهم من النبوة ما وهب ويدخل فيه المال والجاه والأتباع والنسل الطاهر والذرية الطيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A “lofty tongue of truth” means good praise; tongue stands for speech as hand can stand for a gift, fulfilling Abraham’s prayer.
rows.anchor: ولسان الصدق الثناء الحسن وعبر باللسان عما يوجد باللسان ، كما عبر باليد عما يعطي باليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham became an exemplar claimed by all religious communities, as reflected in the commands to follow his way.
rows.anchor: فصيره قدوة حتى ادعاه أهل الأديان كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Abraham separated from people and their idols, God blessed his descendants with Isaac and Jacob, both prophets.
rows.anchor: إن الخليل اعتزل عن الخلق على ما قال : { وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Abraham disavowed his father for God, God named him the father of the Muslims.
rows.anchor: أنه تبرأ من أبيه في الله تعالى على ما قال : { فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Abraham laid his son down to sacrifice him, God ransomed the son with a great sacrifice.
rows.anchor: تل ولده للجبين ليذبحه على ما قال : { فلما أسلما وتله للجبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Abraham surrendered himself to God, God made the fire cool and safe for him.
rows.anchor: فجعل الله تعالى النار عليه بردا وسلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Abraham cared for this community and prayed for a messenger among them, God included him in the blessings of the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: أشفق على هذه الأمة فقال : { ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the matter of Sarah, Abraham was described as faithful, and God made his footprint a blessed place of prayer.
rows.anchor: في حق سارة في قوله : { وإبراهيم الذى وفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Abraham opposed all creatures for God, God took him as an intimate friend, demonstrating that no one loses by serving God.
rows.anchor: عادى كل الخلق في الله فقال : { فإنهم عدو لى إلا رب العالمين

none: Story heading and Quran text only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the fatḥa reading, mukhlaṣ means chosen and selected by God; with kasra, it means sincerely devoted to worshipping God alone.
rows.anchor: أنه كان مخلصا فإذا قرىء بفتح اللام فهو من الإصطفاء والإختباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both Qur’anic readings are established and certain, and God attributed both meanings to Moses.
rows.anchor: ومتى ورد القرآن بقراءتين فكل واحدة منهما ثابت مقطوع به ، فجعل الله تعالى من صفة موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu‘tazilites claim messenger and prophet are coextensive: every messenger is a prophet and every prophet a messenger.
rows.anchor: لكن المعتزلة زعموا كونهما متلازمين فكل رسول نبي وكل نبي رسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messenger and prophet are distinct descriptions; some people deny the Mu‘tazilite equivalence, and the author refers readers to his discussion in al-Hajj.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من أنكر ذلك وقد بينا الكلام فيه في سورة الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ayman means the right side or direction; it may describe the mountain itself or its side.
rows.anchor: من اليمين أي من ناحية اليمين والأيمن صفة الطور أو الجانب

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya interprets nearness as spatial: God brought Moses so near that he heard the pen writing the Torah on the tablets.
rows.anchor: عن أبي العالية قربه حتى سمع صرير القلم حيث كتبت التوراة في الألواح

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The judge prefers nearness of rank and honor, since customary references to nearness to God mean status; worshippers and favored angels are likewise called near.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : وهذا أقرب لأن استعمال القرب في الله قد صار بالتعارف لا يراد به إلا المنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of najiyyan is that Moses was rescued from his enemies.
rows.anchor: وقربناه نجيا } فقيل فيه أنجيناه من أعدائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najiyyan more properly describes private conversation or intimate address.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو من المناجاة في المخاطبة وهو أولى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Aaron was older than Moses.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : كان هرون عليه السلام أكبر من موسى عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God granted Moses Aaron’s prophethood, not Aaron’s person or their brotherhood.
rows.anchor: وإنما وهب الله له نبوته لا شخصه وأخوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron’s appointment answered Moses’ prayer for a minister and brother, confirmed by God’s acceptance of the request and promise to strengthen him through his brother.
rows.anchor: وذلك إجابة لدعائه في قوله : { واجعل لى وزيرا من أهلى * هارون * أخى * اشدد به أزرى

none: Story heading and Quran text only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ismail praised here is Ismail, son of Abraham.
rows.anchor: هذا هو إسماعيل بن إبراهيم عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being true to God’s promise means never disobeying any command conveyed by God’s messenger; receiving revelation itself implies a commitment to carry it out.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد فيما بينه وبين الله تعالى ويمكن أن يكون المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Ismail always fulfilled promises made to people; Ibn Abbas reports he waited a year for a friend who had promised to meet him.
rows.anchor: وروى عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه وعد صاحبا له أن ينتظره في مكان فانتظره سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismail kept his promise to endure the sacrifice, saying he would be patient by God’s will.
rows.anchor: من نفسه الصبر على الذبح فوفى به حيث قال : { ستجدنى إن شاء الله من الصابرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jesus promised a man to wait; the man forgot, but Jesus stayed at the meeting place.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن عيسى عليه السلام قال له رجل : انتظرني حتى آتيك فقال عيسى عليه السلام : نعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says he waited from midmorning until near sunset for a man who forgot their appointment.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( أنه واعد رجلا ونسي ذلك الرجل فانتظره من الضحى إلى قريب

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha‘bi says a daytime appointment should be kept for the whole day and a nighttime appointment for the whole night.
rows.anchor: وسئل الشعبي عن الرجل يعد ميعادا إلى أي وقت ينتظره فقال : إن واعده نهارا فكل النهار وإن واعده

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن زيد
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Zayd says to wait from one prayer time until the next when an appointment is made at prayer time.
rows.anchor: وسئل إبراهيم بن زيد عن ذلك فقال : إذا واعدته في وقت الصلاة فانتظره إلى وقت صلاة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahl can mean everyone to whom Ismail was responsible for conveying the law, namely his whole community, if prayer and almsgiving are obligatory here.
rows.anchor: والأقرب في الأهل أن المراد به من يلزمه أن يؤدي إليه الشرع فيدخل فيه كل أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If prayer and almsgiving mean recommended acts, ahl instead means people in his household, whom he urged to night prayer and cared for spiritually above worldly welfare.
rows.anchor: فإن حمل على الندب فيهما كان المراد أنه كما كان يتهجد بالليل يأمر أهله أي من كان في داره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may have begun with his family to make them models of upright worship, following commands to warn and guide one’s kin and household.
rows.anchor: كان يبدأ بأهله في الأمر بالصلاح والعبادة ليجعلهم قدوة لمن سواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His household had the strongest claim to religious beneficence, just as they have the strongest claim to charitable giving.
rows.anchor: فهم أحق أن يتصدق عليهم فوجب أن يكونوا بالإحسان الديني أولى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets zakat as obedience to God and sincerity, what purifies the worshipper before God.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنها طاعة الله تعالى والاخلاص فكأنه تأوله على ما يزكو به الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense, when zakat is paired with prayer, is obligatory alms; Ismail either directed his eligible family to pay or encouraged voluntary charity.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه إذا قرنت الزكاة إلى الصلاة أن يراد بها الصدقات الواجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being accepted by his Lord is the highest praise: he attained the highest ranks through all his acts of obedience.
rows.anchor: وهو في نهاية المدح لأن المرضى عند الله هو الفائز في كل طاعاته بأعلى الدرجات

none: Story heading and Quran text only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idris is Noah’s great-grandfather in the genealogy Noah son of Lamak, Methuselah, and Akhnukh; Idris was called so for extensive study, and his name was Akhnukh.
rows.anchor: أن إدريس عليه السلام هو جد أبي نوح عليه السلام وهو نوح بن لمك بن متوشلخ بن أخنوخ قيل سمي إدريس لكثرة دراسته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God describes Idris as truthful and a prophet, qualities explained earlier in the commentary.
rows.anchor: ووصفه الله تعالى بأمور : أحدها : أنه كان صديقا . وثانيها : أنه كان نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A figurative interpretation makes Idris’s elevation one of rank, like Muhammad’s raised renown; he was honored with prophethood and thirty scriptures and credited with writing, astronomy, arithmetic, and tailoring.
rows.anchor: أنه من رفعة المنزلة كقوله تعالى لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم : { ورفعنا لك ذكرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers literal elevation to a high location, since “place” alongside “raised” indicates spatial elevation rather than rank.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن المراد به الرفعة في المكان إلى موضع عال وهذا أولى ، لأن الرفعة المقرونة بالمكان تكون رفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Idris was raised alive to heaven and Paradise without dying; others say he was raised to heaven and died there.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم إن الله رفعه إلى السماء وإلى الجنة وهو حي لم يمت ، وقال آخرون : بل رفع إلى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas asked Ka‘b about the verse; Ka‘b recounts that an angel carried Idris to the fourth heaven, where the Angel of Death took his soul after finding him there as ordered.
rows.anchor: كعبا عن قوله : { ورفعناه مكانا عليا } قال : جاءه خليل له من الملائكة فسأله حتى يكلم ملك الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God praises Idris’s ascent because heaven is customarily reached only by those of great rank and stature, as the description of angels also shows.
rows.anchor: إنما مدحه بأن رفعه إلى السماء لأنه جرت العادة أن لا يرفع إليها إلا من كان عظيم القدر والمنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those” refers to the prophets just discussed, from Zechariah through Idris, whom God blessed with prophethood and the other qualities already described.
rows.anchor: وأولئك إشارة إلى المذكورين / في السورة من لدن زكريا إلى إدريس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse groups the prophets by lineage: Idris descended from Adam before Noah; Abraham from Noah’s son Sam; Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob from Abraham; and Moses, Aaron, Zechariah, John, and Jesus through Israel, including Jesus maternally.
rows.anchor: والذي يختص بأنه من ذرية آدم دون من حمل مع نوح هو إدريس عليه السلام ، فقد كان سابقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This ordering indicates that the prophets’ excellence derives both from their deeds and from descent from these prophets.
rows.anchor: فرتب الله سبحانه وتعالى أحوال الأنبياء عليهم السلام الذين ذكرهم على هذا الترتيب منبها بذلك على أنهم كما فضلوا بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were guided and chosen because God guided them to these ranks and selected them for the message.
rows.anchor: اختصوا بهذه المنازل لهداية الله تعالى لهم ، ولأنه اختارهم للرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fall in prostration and weeping in humility, awe, caution, and fear whenever God’s revealed books are recited to them.
rows.anchor: يخرون سجدا وبكيا خضوعا وخشوعا وحذرا وخوفا ، والمراد بآيات الله ما خصهم الله تعالى به من الكتب

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim restricts the verses to passages describing punishment sent down on unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم المراد بالآيات التي فيها ذكر العذاب المنزل بالكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That restriction is remote: passages about Paradise, Hell, promises, threats, encouragement, and warning can all properly induce prostration and tears.
rows.anchor: وهو بعيد لأن سائر الأيات التي فيها ذكر الجنة والنار إلى غير ذلك أولى أن يسجدوا عنده ويبكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported meanings of prostration include prayer, the prescribed prostration of recitation, and general humility; the apparent sense is a specific prostration at recitation.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا فقال بعضهم في السجود : إنه الصلاة وقال بعضهم : المراد سجود التلاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specific prostration may be the Qur’anic prostration of recitation, or a prostration they were prescribed to perform when afraid while hearing the text.
rows.anchor: ثم يحتمل أن يكون المراد سجود التلاوة للقرآن ويحتمل أنهم عند الخوف كانوا قد تعبدوا بالسجود

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses bukiyyan as the plural of “weeping person,” like the plurals for witness and one seated.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج في بكيا : جمع باك مثل شاهد وشهود وقاعد وقعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects taking bukiyyan as a verbal noun: it coordinates with sujjadan, which is a plural of prostrators, so bukiyyan is likewise plural.
rows.anchor: ومن قال في بكيا إنه مصدر فقد أخطأ لأن سجدا جمع ساجد وبكيا معطوف عليه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet urges people to recite the Qur’an and weep, or to make themselves weep if they cannot.
rows.anchor: اتلو القرآن وابكوا فإن لم تبكوا فتباكوا

rows.speaker: صالح المري
rows.claim: Salih al-Marri reports that in a dream the Prophet praised his recitation but asked where its weeping was.
rows.anchor: وعن صالح المري قال : قرأت القرآن عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في المنام فقال لي : يا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says not to hurry to prostrate at the al-Isra prostration; if the eyes do not weep, the heart should.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما إذا قرأتم سجدة سبحان فلا تعجلوا بالسجود حتى تبكوا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says the Qur’an came down with sorrow, so it should be recited sorrowfully.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( القرآن نزل بحزن فاقرأوه بحزن

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says a body from which an eye waters in fear of God is forbidden to the Fire.
rows.anchor: ما اغرورقت عين به بماء إلا حرم الله على النار جسدها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that one who weeps from fear of God will not enter the Fire.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه : ( لا يلج النار من بكى من خشية الله

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars recommend a distinct supplication at each prostration: at al-Tanzil, ask to be a praising prostrator and seek refuge from arrogance.
rows.anchor: فإن قرأ آية تنزيل السجدة قال : اللهم اجعلني من الساجدين لوجهك المسبحين بحمدك

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: At the al-Isra prostration, scholars recommend asking God to make one weep and be humble.
rows.anchor: وإن قرأ سجدة سبحان قال : اللهم اجعلني من الباكين إليك الخاشعين لك

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: At this prostration, scholars recommend asking to be among the blessed, guided servants who prostrate and weep at recitation.
rows.anchor: وإن قرأ هذه السجدة قال : اللهم اجعلني من عبادك المنعم عليهم المهتدين الساجدين لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After praising the prophets to encourage emulation, God describes their successors as their opposite; khalaf with fatḥa denotes bad successors, while khilf with sukūn denotes good successors.
rows.anchor: لما وصف هؤلاء الأنبياء بصفات المدح ترغيبا لنا في التأسي بطريقتهم ذكر بعدهم من هو بالضد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains the spelling distinction using the idioms for a successor to good news and one to evil, then cites a hadith and Labid’s verse about the bad successor left behind.
rows.anchor: ثم قيل في عقب الخبر خلف بفتح اللام وفي عقب الشر خلف بالسكون ، كما قالوا : وعد في ضمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neglecting prayer opposes the previous prophets’ prostration; following desires opposes their weeping, which showed fear.
rows.anchor: فإضاعة الصلاة في مقابلة قوله : { خروا سجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer may be squandered by omitting it altogether or by delaying it beyond its time; complete omission is the more apparent sense.
rows.anchor: تركها قد يكون بأن لا تفعل أصلا وقد يكون بأن لا تفعل في وقتها وإن كان الأظهر هو الأول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies those following desires as Jews who abandoned obligatory prayer, drank wine, and permitted marriage to a paternal half-sister.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما هم اليهود تركوا الصلاة المفروضة وشربوا الخمر واستحلوا نكاح الأخت من الأب

rows.speaker: some scholars
rows.claim: Some infer from the exception “except one who repents and believes” that abandoning prayer makes a person an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: واحتج بعضهم بقوله : { إلا من تاب وءامن } على أن تارك الصلاة كافر

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The author’s school cites the coordination of faith and righteous deeds as proof that faith is distinct from deeds.
rows.anchor: واحتج أصحابنا بها في أن الإيمان غير العمل لأنه تعالى قال : { وامن وعمل صالحا } فعطف العمل على الإيمان

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Ka‘bi answers that good works may still be part of faith even though the verse coordinates them with faith, just as repentance is distinct from faith.
rows.anchor: أجاب الكعبي عنه : بأنه تعالى فرق بين التوبة والإيمان والتوبة من الإيمان فكذلك العمل الصالح يكون من الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls al-Ka‘bi’s answer weak: repentance is a resolve to stop while faith is acknowledgment of God, so their coordination establishes difference; the same applies to works and faith.
rows.anchor: وهذا الجواب ضعيف لأن عطف الإيمان على التوبة يقتضي وقوع المغايرة بينهما لأن التوبة عزم على الترك والإيمان إقرار بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One Arabic usage makes ghayy a general term for evil and rashad for good; an unnamed poet illustrates the contrast with praise for good and blame for straying.
rows.anchor: فمن يلق خيرا يحمد الناس أمره … ومن يغو لا يعدم على الغي لائما

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says “meet ghayy” means meet the punishment for error, like “meet atham” means receive punishment for sins.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : { يلقون غيا } أي يلقون جزاء الغي ، كقوله تعالى : { يلق أثاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations take ghayy as deviation from the path to Paradise or as a valley in Hell from which Hell’s valleys seek refuge.
rows.anchor: غيا عن طريق الجنة . ورابعها : الغي واد في جهنم يستعيذ منه أوديتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first two linguistic explanations are stronger; even if Hell contains a place called Ghayy, that does not displace the ordinary linguistic sense.
rows.anchor: والوجهان الأولان أقرب فإن كان في جهنم موضع يسمى بذلك جاز ولا يخرج من أن يكون المراد ما قدمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning concerns those who do not repent; those who repent, believe, and do good enter Paradise without any injustice.
rows.anchor: ثم بين سبحانه أن هذا الوعيد فيمن لم يتب ، وأما من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فلهم الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says the verse appears to require all three conditions, although someone who repents from unbelief before prayer time, or a menstruating woman, may die without a required deed and still be saved.
rows.anchor: لأن من تاب عن كفره ولم يدخل وقت الصلاة ، أو كانت المرأة حائضا فإنه لا يجب عليها الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer is that these cases are rare; the verse describes the usual case.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الصورة نادرة ، والمراد منه الغالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second objection argues that “they will not be wronged” suggests deserved recompense, impossible if all reward is sheer grace.
rows.anchor: هذا إنما يصح لو كان الثواب مستحقا على العمل ، لأنه لو كان الكل بالتفضل لاستحال حصول الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply is that God uses the language of injustice analogically because the reward resembles a deserved wage.
rows.anchor: أنه لما أشبهه أجرى على حكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adn means abiding; these gardens endure, unlike worldly gardens whose appearance changes as leaves, blossoms, and fruit change.
rows.anchor: والعدن الإقامة وصفها بالدوام على خلاف حال الجنان في الدنيا التي لا تدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In the unseen” may mean Paradise is absent from the people promised it, or they are absent from Paradise and cannot yet see it.
rows.anchor: وهي غائبة عنهم غير حاضرة أو هم غائبون عنها لا يشاهدونها

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim reads the phrase as promising the gardens to those who worship God privately, unlike hypocrites who worship outwardly but not inwardly.
rows.anchor: أن المراد وعد الرحمن للذين يكونون عبادا بالغيب أي الذين يعبدونه في السر بخلاف المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading is stronger: God’s promise concerns what is unseen, and the next phrase assures believers that this unseen promise is effectively present and certain.
rows.anchor: والوجه الأول : أقوى لأنه تعالى بين أن الوعد منه تعالى وإن كان بأمر غائب فهو كأنه مشاهد حاصل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains ma’tiyyan through reciprocal usage: whatever reaches you can be said to have been reached by you, so people come to the promised Garden.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : كل ما وصل إليك فقد وصلت إليه وما أتاك فقد أتيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assurance that the promise is “coming” confirms in people’s hearts the certainty of God’s promise even though its object is unseen.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من قوله : { إنه كان وعده مأتيا } بيان أن الوعد منه تعالى وإن كان بأمر غائب فهو كأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laghw is speech that should be discarded, especially objectionable speech; Paradise’s freedom from it teaches people to avoid idle talk now.
rows.anchor: واللغو من الكلام ما سبيله أن يلغي ويطرح وهو المنكر من القول ونظيره قوله : { لا تسمع فيها لاغية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because greetings for safety seem unnecessary to inhabitants already safe, they might appear idle, except that they serve to honor one another.
rows.anchor: أن معنى السلام هو الدعاء بالسلامة وأهل الجنة لا حاجة بهم إلى هذا الدعاء فكان ظاهره من باب اللغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second solution is to treat the exception of “peace” from idle speech as a disconnected exception.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أن يحمل ذلك على الاستثناء المنقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third solution treats the construction like the poetic exception “there is no fault in them except their swords have nicks.”
rows.anchor:
وثالثها : أن يكون هذا من جنس قول الشاعر :
ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greetings may come from one Paradise resident to another, from the angels, or from God, as in the cited descriptions of greeting and peace.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك السلام يحتمل أن يكون من سلام بعضهم على بعض أو من تسليم الملائكة أو من تسليم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the morning-and-evening provision appeals to what different peoples loved: Persian gold and silk, Yemeni canopied couches, and Arab breakfast and dinner.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن أراد الله تعالى أن يرغب كل قوم بما أحبوه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, morning and evening is an idiom for continuous provision, not a restriction to two times.
rows.anchor: أن المراد دوام الرزق كما تقول أنا عند فلان صباحا ومساء وبكرة وعشيا تريد الدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Paradise has no sun or morning and evening, people may eat at times equivalent to dawn and dusk without those periods literally existing there.
rows.anchor: المراد أنهم يأكلون عند مقدار الغداة والعشي إلا أنه ليس في الجنة غدوة وعشي إذ لا ليل فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that God provides a marker corresponding to a day so residents know the measures of morning and evening.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل ما قيل إنه تعالى جعل لقدر اليوم علامة يعرفون بها مقادير الغداة والعشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase simply means they receive provision whenever they wish, as people customarily do in the morning and evening.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد لهم رزقهم متى شاءوا كما جرت العادة في الغداة والعشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That Garden” uses a demonstrative for a remote, unseen Paradise.
rows.anchor: هذه الإشارة إنما صحت لأن الجنة غائبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We bequeath” may be a metaphor for preserving their Garden as an heir preserves an inheritance.
rows.anchor: نورث استعارة أي نبقي عليه الجنة كما نبقي على الوارث مال المورث

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God transfers the places that would have belonged to the disobedient had they obeyed, and gives them to the pious.
rows.anchor: أن المراد أنا ننقل تلك المنازل ممن لو أطاع لكانت له إلى عبادنا الذين اتقوا ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading is that the pious inherit the lasting fruit of their obedience after their deeds themselves have ended.
rows.anchor: وقد انقضت أعمالهم وثمراتها باقية وهي الجنة فإذا أدخلهم / الجنة فقد أورثهم من تقواهم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The judge infers that Paradise is restricted to the pious, so a major sinner cannot be called pious and cannot enter it.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : فيه دلالة على أن الجنة يختص بدخولها من كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says the pious enter Paradise but does not say others cannot; major sinners are pious in relation to disbelief, so the wording more strongly supports their admission than their exclusion.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على أن المتقي يدخلها وليس فيها دلالة على أن غير المتقي لا يدخلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A stylistic objection asks why the angels’ words are coordinated with God’s speech in the preceding verse without a separator; a clear contextual cue makes this acceptable.
rows.anchor: في الآية إشكالا وهو أو قوله : { تلك الجنة التى نورث من عبادنا من كان تقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that clear contextual clues allow such coordination, as in the transition from God’s speech to Jesus’ words in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: أنه إذا كانت القرينة ظاهرة لم يقبح كما أن قوله سبحانه : { إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent speaker is a group addressing one person, fitting the angels who descend to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك } خطاب جماعة لواحد وذلك لا يليق إلا بالملائكة الذين ينزلون على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported occasion says Quraysh sent five men to the Jews, who advised asking Muhammad about the youths of the Cave, Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; he promised an answer without saying God willing, and revelation was delayed for forty or fifteen days.
rows.anchor: فاحتبس الوحي عنه أربعين يوما وقيل خمسة عشر يوما فشق عليه ذلك مشقة شديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delay distressed Muhammad, and the polytheists said his Lord had abandoned or hated him; Gabriel explained that he descends only when sent and stays back when held back.
rows.anchor: وقال المشركون ودعه ربه وقلاه ، فنزل جبريل عليه السلام فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أبطأت عني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This account connects the verse with the command not to promise a future act without God’s will and with the revelation of al-Duha.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية وأنزل قوله : { ولا تقولن لشىء إنى فاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ “what is before us, behind us, and between” may mean every time—past, future, and present—or this world, the Hereafter, and what lies between.
rows.anchor: أي هو المدبر لنا في كل الأوقات الماضي والمستقبل وما بينهما أو الدنيا والآخرة وما بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These phrases emphasize that God manages angels and all affairs through His will, wisdom, and command, with no one entitled to object.
rows.anchor: والغرض أن أمرنا موكول إلى الله تعالى يتصرف فينا بحسب مشيئته وإرادته وحكمته لا اعتراض لأحد عليه فيه

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim proposes that Paradise’s inhabitants speak: they descend to Paradise only by God’s command; before them is their future in Paradise, behind them their worldly past, and between the two the intervening period.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون قول أهل الجنة والمراد وما نتنزل الجنة إلا بأمر ربك له ما بين أيدينا أي في الجنة مستقبلا

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: On Abu Muslim’s reading, “your Lord is never forgetful” begins God’s address to the Messenger and assures that resurrection will not be forgotten.
rows.anchor: وما كان ربك نسيا لشيء مما خلق فيترك إعادته لأنه عالم الغيب لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says tanazzul means either descending gradually or descent generally; the gradual sense fits repeated angelic descents over time.
rows.anchor: التنزل على معنيين : أحدهما : النزول على مهل . والثاني : بمعنى النزول على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the gradual sense: angels descend at intervals only when God commands.
rows.anchor: واللائق بمثل هذا الموضع هو النزول على مهل والمراد أن نزولنا في الأحايين وقتا بعد وقت ليس إلا بأمر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Before us, behind us, and between” can mean all directions and the angels’ current place; they cannot move between heaven and earth except by God’s order.
rows.anchor: له ما قدامنا وما خلفنا من الجهات وما نحن فيه فلا نتمالك أن ننتقل من جهة إلى جهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading assigns the phrases to worldly events past, future events of the Hereafter, and the forty years between the two trumpet blasts.
rows.anchor: ما سلف من أمر الدنيا وما خلفنا ما يستقبل من أمر الآخرة وما بين ذلك وما بين النفختين وهو أربعون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings are past and remaining lifespan with the present, or the period before existence and after annihilation.
rows.anchor: ما مضى من أعمارنا وما غبر من ذلك والحال التي نحن فيها . ورابعها : ما قبل وجودنا وما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading locates the phrases in the terrain: earth before the descending angels, heaven behind them, and the space between.
rows.anchor: الأرض التي بين أيدينا إذا نزلنا والسماء التي وراءنا وما بين السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every interpretation conveys that God encompasses all things and nothing is hidden from Him; angels therefore act only by His command and judgment.
rows.anchor: فالمقصود أنه المحيط بكل شيء لا تخفى عليه خافية ولا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة فكيف نقدم على فعل إلا بأمره وحكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your Lord is not forgetful” means God has not abandoned Muhammad, as al-Duha says He neither forsook nor hated him; revelation paused because no command to descend had been given.
rows.anchor: أي تاركا لك كقوله : { ما * وعدك * ربك وما قلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord of the heavens and earth cannot forget, since He must continuously sustain them or their order and all dependent existence would collapse.
rows.anchor: فالمراد أن من يكون ربا لها أجمع لا يجوز عليه النسيان إذ لا بد من أن يمسكها حالا بعد حال

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The author’s school uses God’s lordship over everything between heaven and earth to argue that human acts are created by God.
rows.anchor: واحتج / أصحابنا بهذه الآية على أن فعل العبد خلق الله تعالى ، لأن فعل العبد حاصل بين السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses “Lord of the heavens and earth” either as an apposition to “your Lord” or as the predicate of an omitted “He is.”
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : رب السموات والأرض بدل من ربك ويجوز أن يكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command directs Muhammad to worship and persevere through the hardships of religious duties, conveying the message, and his own worship despite sophistries and mockery over delayed revelation.
rows.anchor: فهو أمر للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بالعبادة والمصابرة على مشاق التكاليف في الأداء والإبلاغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Persevere for His worship” uses li rather than ‘ala because worship is like an opponent a fighter must withstand; worship brings hardship, so one must stay firm.
rows.anchor: لأن العبادة جعلت بمنزلة القرن في قولك للمحارب اصطبر لقرنك أي اثبت له فيما يورد عليك من شداته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads “Do you know anyone like Him?” as grounding worship and perseverance in God’s uniqueness and incomparable beneficence through creating bodies, life, intellect, and other fundamental blessings.
rows.anchor: والأقرب هو كونه منعما بأصول النعم وفروعها وهي خلق الأجسام والحياة والعقل وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God has no namesake or partner in His name; idols may be called gods, but no one else is called Allah, and Ibn Abbas says no one else is called al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : المراد أنه سبحانه ليس له شريك في اسمه وبينوا ذلك من وجهين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says no one besides God is named al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لا يسمى بالرحمن غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the namesake-only explanation and says the more sound meaning is that no one shares God’s unique creative beneficence, which obligates supreme worship.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول هو الصواب والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding worship and perseverance, God answers the objection that worship has no worldly benefit and that some deny the Hereafter by presenting proof for resurrection.
rows.anchor: لما أمر بالعبادة والمصابرة عليها فكأن سائلا سأل وقال هذه العبادات لا منفعة فيها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier’s question about being brought back alive after death is spoken as denial and incredulous rejection.
rows.anchor: وإما قالوا ذلك على وجه الإنكار والاستبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The human” may mean humanity generally: a statement made by some members can be attributed to the whole group, and every person initially has this natural doubt until evidence overrides it.
rows.anchor: المراد الجنس بأسره فإن قيل كلهم غير قائلين بذلك فكيف يصح هذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse refers to a specific person—Abu Jahl or Ubayy ibn Khalaf—or to the class of unbelievers who deny resurrection.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالإنسان شخص معين فقيل : هو أبو جهل ، وقيل : هو أبي بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer is that God first created the human from nothing, so recreating him is possible and easier than the original creation.
rows.anchor: إذ لا شك أن الإعادة ثانيا أهون من الإيجاد أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says no one could give a shorter proof of resurrection than this and cites other verses stating that the one who originated creation will revive it.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العلماء : لو اجتمع كل الخلائق على إيراد حجة في البعث على هذا الاختصار لما قدروا عليها

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The author’s school argues that nonexistence is not a thing, based on the description of the human as previously not being anything.
rows.anchor: واحتج أصحابنا بهذه الآية على أن المعدوم ليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls that proof weak: the human is an aggregate of elements and accidents, and showing the aggregate was nothing does not show each constituent was nothing.
rows.anchor: ضعيف لأن الإنسان عبارة عن مجموع جواهر متألفة قامت بها أعراض وهذا المجموع ما كان شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though remembering usually means knowledge once acquired and later forgotten, here it means reflect and come to know, especially under the intensified reading.
rows.anchor: المراد أو لا يتفكر فيعلم خصوصا إذا قرىء أو لا يذكر الإنسان بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the light reading, the command means to recognize one’s own history: everyone knows they once were not alive and later became alive.
rows.anchor: أما إذا قرىء أو لا يذكر بالتخفيف فالمراد أو لا يعلم ذلك من حال نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath both reinforces the truth of the report, as customary oaths do, and magnifies Muhammad by attaching God’s name to his; compare the oath by heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: وفائدة القسم أمران : أحدهما : أن العادة جارية بتأكيد الخبر باليمين . والثاني : أن في إقسام الله تعالى باسمه مضافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction before “the devils” can mean “and” or “together with”; accompaniment better expresses that each unbeliever is chained with the demon who misled him.
rows.anchor: والواو في { الشياطين } ويجوز أن تكون للعطف وأن تكون بمعنى مع وهي بمعنى مع أوقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering around Hell precedes entry, and being on their knees depicts the unbelievers as humiliated or helpless.
rows.anchor: وهذا الإحضار يكون قبل إدخالهم جهنم ثم إنه تعالى يحضرهم على أذل صورة لقوله تعالى : { جثيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although every community kneels, perhaps from customary supplication before kings or overwhelming distress, the unbelievers’ added humiliation is that they remain kneeling from resurrection until judgment.
rows.anchor: لعل المراد أنهم يكونون من وقت الحشر إلى وقت الحضور في الموقف على هذه الحالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shi‘a is a faction or group following a misguided leader; the word is like firqa and fi’a.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالشيعة وهي فعلة كفرقة وفئة الطائفة التي شاعت أي تبعت غاويا من الغواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will extract the most rebellious from each faction for more severe punishment, because leaders who mislead, defiant innovators, and those who spread false arguments deserve more than blind followers.
rows.anchor: فمن كان أشدهم تمردا في كفره خص بعذاب أعظم لأن عذاب الضال المضل يجب أن يكون فوق عذاب من يضل تبعا لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone is punished; the extraction distinguishes intensity of punishment, not who receives punishment at all, as “more deserving” presumes shared punishment.
rows.anchor: ففائدة هذه التمييز التخصيص بشدة العذاب لا التخصيص بأصل العذاب

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says ayyuhum is raised as a quotation: God extracts those who are said to be the most rebellious.
rows.anchor: فعن الخليل أنه مرتفع على الحكاية تقديره لننزعن الذين يقال فيهم أيهم أشد

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says ayyuhum is built on ḍamma because the opening of its embedded clause was dropped; with the full clause “which of them is most rebellious,” it would be inflected.
rows.anchor: وسيبويه على أنه مبني على الضم لسقوط صدر الجملة التي هي صلة حتى لو جيء به لأعرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some restrict “none of you” to the previously mentioned unbelievers, switching from third-person reference to direct address; they argue believers cannot approach Hell.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم المراد من تقدم ذكره من الكفار فكنى عنهم أولا كناية الغيبة ثم خاطب خطاب المشافهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restricted reading cites the promise that the saved are kept far from Hell, do not hear its sound, and are secure from the terror of that Day.
rows.anchor: إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators read the verse universally for believers and unbelievers, since its unqualified wording does not exclude anyone and the next verse rescues the Godfearing from among those who arrived.
rows.anchor: وقال الأكثرون : إنه عام في كل مؤمن وكافر لقوله تعالى : { وإن منكم إلا واردها } فلم يخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence “then We save the Godfearing and leave the wrongdoers there” entails that all are among those who arrive at Hell.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يقال : { ثم ننجى الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا } إلا والكل واردون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says none who fought at Badr or Hudaybiyya will enter Hell; when Hafsa asks how this fits the verse, the Prophet answers, “Then We save the Godfearing.”
rows.anchor: لا يدخل النار أحد شهد بدرا والحديبية فقالت حفصة : أليس الله يقول : { وإن منكم إلا واردها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes arrival as coming near Hell to the place of accounting, not entering it; God then keeps the pious far away as in al-Anbiya.
rows.anchor: الورود الدنو من جهنم وأن يصيروا حولها وهو موضع المحاسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word warada can mean approaching without entering: the water-drawer approaches water, Moses came upon the water of Midian, and a caravan may arrive at a town without entering it.
rows.anchor: واحتجوا على أن الورود قد يراد به القرب بقوله تعالى : { فأرسلوا واردهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading humans and jinn gather around Hell; the decree is a settled obligation under the threat, and God removes the pious from it.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا معنى الآية أن الجن والإنس يحضرون حول جهنم : { كان على ربك حتما مقضيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry reading cites “you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell” and “Pharaoh leads his people to the Fire”; their wurood means entering it.
rows.anchor: وقال : { فأوردهم النار وبئس الورد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those kept far away would only need to be removed if they were already in Hell; leaving the wrongdoers there kneeling likewise implies they entered.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أنهم يبقون في ذلك الموضع الذي وردوه وهم إنما يبقون في النار فلا بد وأن يكونوا قد دخلوا النار

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن رواحة
rows.claim: Ibn Rawaha says God mentions arrival but not departure; the Prophet tells him to read what follows, “then We save the Godfearing,” without rejecting his entry interpretation.
rows.anchor: أخبر الله عن الورود ولم يخبر بالصدور ، فقال عليه السلام : يا ابن رواحة اقرأ ما بعدها ثم ننجي

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir says he heard the Prophet define wurood as entry: every righteous and wicked person enters, and Hell becomes cool and safe for believers, whose cold causes the people’s cries.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : الورود الدخول لا يبقى بر ولا فاجر إلا دخلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proponents say believers enter without fear or harm, with joy: the Hereafter is recompense rather than a testing ground, and reports promise the saved their place in Paradise at death or in the grave.
rows.anchor: المؤمنون يدخلون النار من غير خوف وضرر ألبتة بل مع الغبطة والسرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that Hell includes fireless passages: believers pass through these, while unbelievers enter the burning depths.
rows.anchor: البقعة المسماة بجهنم لا يمتنع أن يكون في خلالها ما لا نار فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the fire is extinguished so believers cross it; they enter as if Hell were melted fat.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ( يردونها كأنها إهالة

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir ibn Abd Allah relates asking the Prophet about Paradise residents’ concern that they had been promised arrival at Hell; they are told they did arrive when it was extinguished.
rows.anchor: وعن جابر بن عبد الله : ( أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إذا دخل أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that fire has no intrinsic heat: God makes the parts touching unbelievers burn, but makes those touching believers cool and safe, as with Abraham.
rows.anchor: أن حرارة النار ليست بطبعها فالأجزاء الملاصقة لأبدان الكفار يجعلها الله عليهم محرقة مؤذية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says one of these three explanations is also needed for the angels assigned to punish, since they must be in the Fire alongside the punished.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه لا بد من أحد هذه الوجوه في الملائكة الموكلين بالعذاب حتى يكونوا في النار مع المعاقبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harmless entry still benefits believers by increasing their joy at escape and intensifying unbelievers’ grief when they see their enemies escape.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك مما يزيدهم سرورا إذا علموا الخلاص منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ presence also publicly humiliates the deniers before the faithful and those who warned them, and lets the believers rebuke them.
rows.anchor: فيه مزيد غم على أهل النار من حيث تظهر فضيحتهم عند المؤمنين بل وعند الأولياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their presence confirms that believers’ warnings and proofs about resurrection were true and that those who denied it were liars.
rows.anchor: أظهروا لهم أنهم كانوا صادقين فيما قالوا ، وأن المكذبين بالحشر والنشر كانوا كاذبين
